The little spinefoot Siganus spinus is a widely distributed herbivorous rabbitfish inhabiting coral reefs and seagrass beds throughout the Indo-Pacific region. Field surveys indicate that adults rarely exceed a maximum total length of 28 cm [Li = 28 cm], a size that positions this species among the medium-bodied members of the family Siganidae. Morphometric data collected from multiple populations across the Philippine archipelago show that the total length at puberty is approximately 12.8 cm [Lp = approximately 12.8 cm], marking the onset of gonadal development and reproductive competence. At this length, individuals typically attain a corresponding wet weight at puberty of 29.54 grams [Wwp = 29.54 grams], reflecting the energetic investment required to reach sexual maturation. Comparative studies with congeneric species suggest that these size thresholds are closely tied to the availability of algal resources on shallow reef flats, where juveniles and sub-adults forage extensively before reaching maturity. The relationship between length and body mass follows a typical allometric scaling pattern for the genus, with the ultimate wet weight at asymptotic size reaching approximately 447 grams [Wwi = approximately 447 grams], a figure derived from extensive length-weight regressions across wild-caught specimens.
